# MeetingRow

One meeting in an agenda. It shows when it starts and for how long, its title, the person's part or answer, one more line and its actions (Join, Chat). A meeting happening now is marked "Now", with a bar at its start edge, and past meetings are quieter, in text that keeps its contrast. Screen readers hear the row by its time and title, and "Now" when it is happening.

```tsx
import { MeetingRow } from "@/registry/ouro/components/ouro/meeting-row/meeting-row";
```

## Example

```tsx
<MeetingRow title="Weekly sync" time="10:00" duration="30 min" state="now" actions={<Button href={joinUrl}>Join</Button>} />
```

## Use instead when

- Use `Item` instead for a row that is not tied to a time, and `Calendar` to choose a date.

## Props

Type: `MeetingRowProps`.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `actions` | `ReactNode` |  | Buttons for the meeting, such as Join and Chat. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Layout only: margins, grid placement (`mt-1`). Appearance classes warn in development. |
| `dateTime` | `string` |  | The start as a machine-readable date and time ("2026-06-01T10:00"), for the `<time>` element. |
| `detail` | `ReactNode` |  | One quiet line under the title ("Ada Lovelace", "Starts in 5 min", "Room 4"). |
| `duration` | `string` |  | How long, already formatted ("30 min"), under the time. |
| `nowLabel` | `string` | `"Now"` | The badge on a meeting happening now, for other languages. |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLElement>` |  | Reaches the rendered element. |
| `state` (required) | `"now" \| "past" \| "upcoming"` |  | `past` rows are quieter, and a `now` row is marked and called out. |
| `status` | `string` |  | The person's part or answer as a short label ("Organizer", "Tentative", "Declined"). Leave it out for a plain yes. |
| `statusTone` | `"primary" \| "secondary" \| "destructive" \| "success" \| "warning"` | `"secondary"` | The status badge's color role from the theme, named after its token. |
| `time` (required) | `string` |  | When it starts, already formatted ("10:00", "9:30 AM"). |
| `title` (required) | `string` |  | The meeting's title. |

## Native attributes

Also accepts the attributes in React's `HTMLAttributes` (`id`, `aria-*`, event handlers), passed to the rendered element, except those named on this page.

## Don't use

These are not props. Passing one fails the type check with the fix in the error, and in development a console message names the fix.

- `start`: Not a prop. The start is `time`: `<MeetingRow time="10:00">`.
- `subject`: Not a prop. The meeting's title is `title`: `<MeetingRow title="Weekly sync">`.

## `className` is for layout only

Pass margins, width and grid placement (`mt-4`, `w-full`, `col-span-2`). Your classes always win over Ouro UI's: MeetingRow merges `className` last with `cn` (tailwind-merge), so a class that conflicts with its own replaces it.[^layout-classes]

Appearance comes from props, not classes. In development, a class that sets appearance logs one warning per component instance, naming the prop to use instead. A class sets appearance when, after its variants (`hover:`, `sm:`) and any `!` are removed, it starts with `bg-`, `text-`, `border-`, `rounded-`, `shadow-`, `font-`, `ring-`, `from-`, `via-`, `to-`, `fill-` or `stroke-`, or is `border`, `rounded`, `shadow` or `ring`, or has a `dark:` variant. Text wrapping, overflow and table layout classes (`text-wrap`, `text-ellipsis`, `border-collapse`) are layout and do not warn.

Alignment classes (`text-center`) warn too: set alignment on a parent element.
